mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline, discretionary trips are suppressed and retail visits stay weak over the next four weeks. This pattern implies continued time at home rather than destination shopping.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its previous 4-week mean for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below baseline and RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GROCERY_PHARM relative to the prior week indicates more errand-based local activity, which spills into nearby retail and recreation spending within one to two weeks. The effect is strongest when GROCERY_PHARM is also above baseline.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after a 3-point or larger week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM on repeated occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and TRANSIT move up together, outdoor and in-town movement expands, creating a broader outing environment that lifts retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks. The signal should be strongest when both series are improving simultaneously.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior 4-week mean after joint weekly gains in PARKS and TRANSIT on at least two occasions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in TRANSIT relative to WORKPLACES indicates commuting disruption or access restrictions, which reduces impulse shopping and mall traffic within one week. Retail-and-recreation should fall quickly when transit mobility breaks down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES does not rise
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after TRANSIT drops more than 5 points while WORKPLACES is flat or lower.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL combined with weak WORKPLACES signals a stay-at-home substitution that keeps retail trips below the prior month average. The drag on RETAIL_REC persists for about four weeks because fewer commuters generate fewer incidental shopping visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 4-week mean even though RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and WORKPLACES remains below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained strengthening in PARKS mobility relative to the prior two weeks signals favorable weather or leisure demand, which then supports retail and recreation visits after a short lag. The effect should appear within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after PARKS rises in back-to-back weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-regulation regime, declining TRANSIT and WORKPLACES together precede weaker retail-and-recreation mobility because fewer trips are made for nonessential purposes. The effect should persist over four weeks rather than just one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its previous 4-week mean for most of the next month after TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both weaken together.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both strengthen while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, local short-trip activity is high but centered on essentials and nearby recreation, not retail shopping. That mix should hold RETAIL_REC down over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are both above their previous week values
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within two weeks despite simultaneous weekly gains in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS and persistent above-baseline RESIDENTIAL.
